title: Microbatching + FlashFuse Kernel Heuristics (draft)
content:
Context and objective:
This is a working note on combining microbatching policies with fused FlashAttention-style kernels (we're calling the fused path "FlashFuse" here) and how those kernels should interact with the paged KV cache. Goal: get stable 95th percentile latency under 40ms for 8k-context GPT-like models on 8xA100 while reducing per-token GPU cycles by 20% relative to current baseline.

High-level constraints we care about:
- Small request size distribution: 60% single-turn short (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (64-512), 10% long (>512)
- Latency SLOs strict for hosted API (p50/p95), throughput matters for Dedicated (reserved pools)
- KV residency fluctuates; paged-KV must avoid thrashing when many small requests touch hot prefixes

Quick summary of FlashFuse approach (draft):
- Fuse query/key/value matmuls + rotary + softmax + dropout into one kernel where possible. Avoid materializing Q/K/V where it increases memory traffic.
- Two kernel code paths keyed on sequence-length *and* batch-size: compact-path (low-latency for small batch and short seq) and bulk-path (throughput-optimized for large microbatches).
- Compact-path uses warp-synchronous reductions, minimal shared memory, low register footprint. Bulk-path uses tiled matmul + shared memory + persistent threads for maximum occupancy.

Microbatching heuristics that schedule requests into these paths:
- If incoming request tokens <= 64 and current queueing latency < 3ms -> schedule to compact-path immediately (no waiting to aggregate).
- If queue length or accumulated tokens across pending requests > microbatch_token_threshold (experiment with 2k/4k/8k) -> flush into bulk-path batching.
- Per-model adaptive backoff: if compact-path p95 starts trending downwards (worse), increase threshold to favor bulk batching; inverse if bulk-path per-token cost increases latency for small requests.
- TTL-based prefix coalescing: group requests sharing same prefix_id (application supplied) into a hot-path microbatch to increase KV cache hits.

Paged KV interactions (residency + prefetching ideas):
- Keep a tiny LRU with hot set metadata on CPU (per-GPU) that tracks suffix usage frequency and last-access; maintain approximate residency map in device memory (bitset + generation counter).
- When scheduling compact-path, prefer requests whose prefixes have resident KV pages (fast path). If prefix misses, optionally trigger an asynchronous prefetch and punt request to bulk-path to amortize page load cost.
- Prefetch policy: prioritize pages referenced by many pending microbatched requests; avoid prefetching pages for single noisy requests unless request latency budget permits (low priority).
- Page eviction heuristic: keep pages that are frequently accessed across models (cross-model hotness) pinned on Dedicated by default; for Hosted, use cost-aware eviction where pages with high load *and* high miss penalty are retained longer.

Kernel implementation notes and tuning knobs:
- Register pressure: fused kernels easily blow registers. We should maintain two compile variants with different max-register constraints (-maxrregcount) and run autotune on representative inputs.
- Shared memory layout: store Q*K tiles in smem for bulk-path; for compact-path rely on warp shuffle to reduce shared memory usage.
- Avoid atomic ops in hot loops; instead use warp-vote + prefix-scan patterns for reductions.
- Use cooperative groups to map token loops to thread blocks for >1024 tokens per block in bulk-path.
- FP16/TF32 baseline; enable int8+KV-quantization path in a separate kernel as fallback. Quantized path must compensate for softmax numerical stability (stabilized softmax with 32-bit accumulators).

Microbench results (toy runs on 8xA100, synthetic traces) - early numbers:
- Compact-path, seq=32, batch=1: 1.8x improvement vs current baseline (mainly due to avoiding QKV materialize + lower mem traffic).
- Bulk-path, aggregated tokens=4096, seq avg=256: 1.5x improvement per-token but higher p50 for single short requests due to waiting ~4ms to batch.
- Prefetching pages for coalesced hot prefixes reduced miss latency by ~60% in hot-path sim, but increased overall memory bandwidth when mispredicted.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Where to place fallback logic: should the scheduler be kernel-aware (explicitly prefer a kernel) or should kernels self-select based on input shapes? I lean toward scheduler-driven selection for visibility and easier metrics.
- How to quantify when a prefetch is worth it? Need an online estimator of expected reuse count per-page weighted by request latency budget.
- Interaction with quantized KV (4-bit/8-bit): how many pages can we store safely on device before numerical drift affects causal attention?
- Error handling: if bulk-path bulk-aggregates and one request fails (cancelled), we need a cheap partial-unwind. We could mark request entries as cancelled and have kernels skip cancelled indices; need to measure branch divergence impact.

Suggested experiments (short-term):
1) Implement compact-path prototype that fuses QKV->attn for seq<=64, single-batch. Measure register usage, occupancy, and p95 on mixed trace. (Owner: Priya)
2) Implement bulk-path tiled fused kernel using persistent threads and cooperative groups; enable microbatch flush based on token budget. (Owner: Diego)
3) KV-prefetch simulator: offline sim that ingests traces and simulates residency + prefetch decisions to compute hit-rate and bandwidth impact. (Owner: Hannah)
4) Autotune harness: parameter sweep for microbatch_token_threshold in {2048,4096,8192}, compact-path wait time in {0,1,3,5}ms, and register caps {64,80,96}. (Owner: Omar)

Operational metrics to expose in Console for tuning:
- Per-kernel p50/p95 latency, per-token GPU cycles, occupancy, shared mem usage
- KV page hit/miss rates by prefix_id
- Microbatch size distribution and average wait time before execution
- Per-model cost delta when opting into FlashFuse vs baseline

Action items (near-term):
- Spin up a branch with compact-path prototype + microbenchmark suite by EOW (Priya).
- Create a short internal benchmark trace that mirrors hosted request size distribution; put into runtime/perf/traces (Diego).
- Draft a one-pager for engineering review on the prefetch budget estimator with simple heuristics (Hannah).

Notes to self:
- Keep the compact-path lean; it's the primary win for our PLG free-tier users.
- Avoid overfitting post-launch to synthetic traces; the autotuner should run periodically on production traces (privacy-safe sampling).

References and related work:
- FlashAttention paper and reference implementations (Huang et al.)
- Prior internal PR: runtime/pull/742 - initial fused attention attempt (mostly tiled matmul approach)
- KV paging design doc in Confluence (linked above)

Unresolved design decisions for review meeting:
- Scheduler-driven kernel binding vs kernel self-selection
- Default prefetch budget for hosted vs dedicated
- E2E rollback strategy in case FlashFuse introduces regressions to rare model shapes

End of notes.

-- Priya
